label: Macnaughton 2019
setting: Vista low vision rehabilitation service, Leicestershire and Rutland (assessed at home 87% or Vista Low Vision Clinic 13%)
diagnosis_mix: AMD 50% (dry 10.17%; wet 20.33%); diabetic retinopathy/maculopathy 5%; hereditary retinal disorder 5%; retinal vascular occlusions 7%; glaucoma 12%; other 21% (self-reported primary cause, Table 1)
recruitment: newly registered (CVI) adults with visual impairment approached at referral to Vista; new to rehabilitation services; excluded if unable to complete assessments in English or cognitively impaired (Six-item Brief Cognitive Screener); sampling method (consecutive vs convenience) and dates NR
notes: Not a diagnostic accuracy study: no sens/spec/AUC; PAI evaluated by Rasch analysis and correlated with clinical and psychosocial measures. n=60 for PAI; ACC n=55, contrast sensitivity n=59 (p5). 47 goals retained after Rasch (p6). Binocular VA, habitual correction, Bailey-Lovie chart (p3). All interviews face to face by one examiner (p3). Time to administer NR.
